column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3d context; a statement of what she holds is, in a court's terms, a comfort letter, so it needs the promise sentence beside it (row 36).
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; the verb decides (We will not against It is our policy), the law's own reason for WORDS' ban on intend, expect, hope and aim for the top.
Tue 17 Nov: store; lenders priced the weaker word (3/8% to 1/2%); the 50,000 pounds a year is a 1990 comment's arithmetic, not the court's.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c or 3d aha and conceit turn (a policy is pencil, rubbed out in the 1985 tin crash); anchor the contrast on IPS l.15's move (money she already owns before the meetings), not on l.17 alone, which is itself a policy a judge could set beside It is our policy; keep the guard that her words do not bind her.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d guard; the fact half of her words must be literally true on the day (bottom held since January 2028, top since the move); never say her words make her liable.
Tue 17 Nov: store, a 3e clause at most; policy lost in London and practice won in Sydney in 1989; read through Gate Gourmet's quotation; say a Sydney court, no Australian flag.
Tue 17 Nov: store; the reader says what it counts (the bank refused a not-a-guarantee line); a practitioner's account, not the law report.
Tue 17 Nov: the same Sydney ruling in secondary quotations only; row 6 carries it.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; will provide and will not be withdrawn, with an end point, were held a promise; supports will give with an amount and a date.

Tue 17 Nov: same point as H7-070 (support promised from someone's will is withdrawn in a downturn), here a corporate parent; H7-070's donor pledges fit 3e better; keep can also fall, never fall together.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; even we will reads as intention when the rest is vague, so will give needs its amount, purpose and date in the same sentence; converges with rows 18 and 26.
Tue 17 Nov: store guard; say a New South Wales court, never Australian law has held; the Australian angle has no place unless it earns one.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d guard; no line disclaiming legal force (it would be read exactly so) and none claiming it; note the tension with Q22-021's use (one line calling it a statement of intent).
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; what counts is how a reasonable listener hears her words; drop which is what the funder test measured, since its four readers were simulated, a rehearsal, not listeners measured.
Tue 17 Nov: store; why US funders treat a signed pledge as near cash (a probability of reliance is enough); read in two verbatim quotations; s.90(2) not widely adopted.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3c background; a signed pledge's legal weight depends on the state; Maryland refused s.90(2).

Tue 17 Nov: store only, not a 3d aha; the parallel breaks: Laura's money also stays hers (held for her, not given) and her statement is no more enforceable, so the difference is markets, not paper; never set the lapsed card against her owned money.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; name the facility as the purpose, not the residency in general; converges with rows 26 and 29.
Tue 17 Nov: store; New Jersey enforces charitable pledges, the state-line contrast with rows 16-17.

Tue 17 Nov: store; the US pledge-law synthesis holds, but funders' box counts a signed one anyway rests on the simulated funder test, not on rows 15-19; re-base it on a real funder definition (Q18-009 counts a pledge only if legally obligated) or drop the clause.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d client knowledge; a Taiwan court read best efforts as no promise; pairs with H6-001; Laura says will give.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c or 3d; the reader's own credit file decided the letter's weight; drop co-sponsors filed Laura's figure as committed as if real funders did: the funder test's readers were simulated.

Tue 17 Nov: store; why Taiwan's companies write comfort letters (Company Act art. 16); art. 16 binds companies, not foundations, and the funder test's corporate-foundation personas were simulated, so no claim about real co-sponsors.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; Taiwan's scholarship sorts letters into confirming a fact and promising to act, academic backing for row 36's two sentences.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d guard from a second legal system; the fact sentence must be correct and complete (held for her, never in her name, never secured); an academic view.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; art. 153's necessary points (amount, purpose, time) make will give a promise, not a moral expectation; the time is the 2033 contribution, paid from Treasuries maturing December 2032.
Tue 17 Nov: store; Taiwan letters of intent judged by content; rulings seen only in a forum article, UNVERIFIED until the Judicial Yuan texts are read.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3e background; even a binding Taiwan gift yields only the gift, no interest or damages (art. 409 para 2); adds to Q55-035; Taiwan law is outside the case's scope.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d; a restricted gift needs words naming the purpose and the receiving body; never suggest an escrow or any legal step for Laura.
Tue 17 Nov: unread mainland China minutes giving the same reasonable-reader test as row 14, which is read at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store; concrete words bound under a soft heading (claim 4); judgment not read at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store, claim 4; French law made the letter of intent a binding security, so the heading decides nothing and courts read the verb.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3e background; a promise to give is weak until paid or notarised in Germany as in Taiwan; never suggest a notary; Laura's strength is money owned.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c and 3d; never secured holds, but this row files the simulated funder test as VERIFIED funder practice; label it a rehearsal with simulated readers and rest what secured means in a funder's office on real definitions (Q18-009, Q22-001, Q32-021, Q75-013).

Tue 17 Nov: 3c or 3d aha (a pledge that can lapse is counted above money she holds); rest it on real funder definitions, not the simulated test; say what is stated is owned whatever markets do, never that the floor fund's payout is fixed; paper not money oversimplifies, since secured also means cash received.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d spine; one fact (what is held for her and since when) plus one promise (she will give the top, $115,000 on today's figures); the law's reason for the bans on intend, expect, at least and up to; fits the settled order.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e clause; the contribution rests on what is owned, never on the words' legal force; fix certain, which takes the stated range as its subject (settled 16 Nov), not the Treasuries or an amount.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d conceit turn (the team's sentence, never Laura's); a comfort letter is pencil dressed as ink, signed and on letterhead, still only a policy; it turns readers' habit of hearing ink as signed into the definition (ink is owned); one turn per part, so this or row 4.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a density; deleting off-topic measures raised best choices 40% to 62%, the evidence for cutting 3a's figures that do not answer its question.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; moving figures to the end did not reliably help, only deletion did, so cut figures go to Figure 1's note or the store, not the part's last sentence.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a-3e; numerate readers gained only from deletion, not reordering; the judges' numeracy is assumed.
Tue 17 Nov: Table 2 highlights one row at most (74% vs 60%); drop an aha or a conceit turn, not both, which contradicts the aha register's pairing and Book 19's conceit developed part by part.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c order; lead with the top co-sponsors count, then the part held since January 2028; an analogy from a scale's direction.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; the headline figure carries its yardstick in the same sentence, and a yardstick is not a secondary figure.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c density; the cushion slope and the 0.75% case are small differences in an unfamiliar field, so they go to Table 2's note; NUMBERS 3 has about $119 per 0.1% and at most $402.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a-3e; the facts box cut words and kept the needed numbers in a small table; supports tables over prose, not cutting figures as such.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; the headline figure must stay in the prose or readers guess (65% overestimated tenfold).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a; one form of the price, but the top-up ($2,388, IPS l.13) and the extra Treasuries ($35,894, the reserve's size) keep their two names in words, so the price is never said as l.13's completion; the split figures may go to Figure 1's note.
Tue 17 Nov: the same do-the-subtraction point as row 18, which carries the direct quote.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a and 3c; a one-line explanation of what a figure means raised good choices (71% vs 59%), support for one basis clause, for use not trust.
Tue 17 Nov: process; three layers (prose, tables and notes, store); lose nothing holds only where each cut has its written reason.
Tue 17 Nov: process; evidence alone did not change a document, so the density rule needs its 27 Nov check.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c; the part held since January 2028 is the one yardstick for the top co-sponsors count.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; compare the chosen standard with one alternative at most (51% to 77%); aha 1's three sizings go to a note.
Tue 17 Nov: 3b-3c; say one side of a split; the parallel is partial, since the plan's sides do not add to a whole.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; when a figure leaves the prose, state its result (most of the extra Treasuries come back by 2042 at today's rates), never its parts.
Tue 17 Nov: process; present what is critical even at the expense of completeness; completeness lives in the tables and the store, each cut with its written reason.
Tue 17 Nov: process for 27 Nov; the numbers owner marks each SKELETON figure prose, table or store; a summary of rows 1 and 16, not new evidence.
Tue 17 Nov: process; readers say they want more and use less; panel 3's judges were simulated, so the evidence is Boyce's readers, not the panel.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c density; computations interspersed in a plain explanation hurt (d about 0.69-0.97), so the rounding and the cut leave the sentence on who owns each end.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c; a mechanic may stay only after the answer, never between its steps.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e; five areas, one sentence each, as a captioned summary; each keeps its step or the summary fails.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; the honest size of the coherence effect, large in labs and small in the field; extra details' costs add.
Tue 17 Nov: conceit and ahas; interesting material held attention; drop the finalist's an aha or a conceit turn, not both, which contradicts the aha register's pairing under Book 19.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; readers average, so a weaker figure or source dilutes the strongest; same paper as Q80-010 (3f); gold nuggets still land in an exhibit's note, never only in the store (Book 19).
Tue 17 Nov: 3c; certain, said of the stated range, reads weaker when its sentence carries the rounding and the fee, so the mechanics stay out of that sentence.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a and 3e; each figure after the fee only, the fee's working in Figure 1's note.
Tue 17 Nov: Table 2; detail helps when it sits in one table, a nuance to Q60-041 from the same study.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e; one number for shares, $95,000 to $140,000 for the top across every start since 1962 (NUMBERS 8i), the rest to Table 2's note.
Tue 17 Nov: Table 2, 3c and 3e; columns labelled by market, never central or moderate, since a short warning did not stop PRIIPs scenarios being read as forecasts.
Tue 17 Nov: an industry body restating the 2015 test's table over histogram and funnel, already Q60-041.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c; the bottom line said plainly on its basis ($115,000 on today's figures), assumptions in Table 2's note on the same page; you would pay over you might pay.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c and 3d; no might in the co-sponsor sentence; one tester's words, agreeing with Book 19.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; name the headline figure in the first sentence and every table in the prose, since half of readers missed examples at the back.
Tue 17 Nov: the same coverage-example finding as row 34, from the advocate's own retrospective; the funder test is no corroboration (simulated readers).
Tue 17 Nov: first sentences of 3a, 3c and 3e; the same notice doubled switching on the front page and had no effect inside, so position matters as much as presence.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a-3e; structure, not length, did the work (2.5 pages no worse than 1), so cut for one answer per part, not for brevity.
Tue 17 Nov: process; both sides of Book 17 in one hearing; each moved figure needs a findable home and a written reason.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; a 250-word paragraph with a caveat in most clauses is the one GOV.UK warns against.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e; detail implies unwarranted accuracy, so say by less than one $5,000 step and move $116,211-$119,478 to Table 2's note; Q71-026 records the counter for experts.
Tue 17 Nov: the 27 Nov test, first sentences of 3a, 3c and 3e only; note the tension with Q14b-029 (a theme sentence without numbers), since the density cut puts the answer and its one figure first.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e; the margins said once together in one place, and prose never repeats Figure 1 or Table 2.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c; core sentence first, conditions as if-then lines in Table 2's note; NUMBERS 3 has about $119 per 0.1%, so about $120 only as its rounding.
Tue 17 Nov: 3a; a second form of the same number added nothing and no word label is needed, support for row 10's one form.
